introduction: Meet Ijale in Mosswood’s village market, prepare an exact large beet, and distinguish recovering or receiving supplies from an accepted trade.
orientation: Arrive in Mosswood through its village road to discover the zone. Meet Ijale to reveal her beet request; the journal keeps current supplies separate from accepted history.
Ask Ijale about hi or hello. Both words lead to the same greeting and request; hearing either does not complete a trade or create a second achievement.
Ijale accepts one exact large beet for the native coin reward. Bring the beet loose in your inventory. A supplied copy also fits without remembered farming, first recovery or a prior greeting.
Large beets are hidden ground stock near the cattle plot and beet fields. Search can reveal surviving stock; finding it and carrying it are separate actions. Another player may already have taken it.
The optional beet row describes what you carry now. Packed supplies need to be taken out before offering. A remembered find, an apple or money cannot replace the exact beet.
Eating the beet uses up that food instead of completing Ijale’s request. An accepted trade uses its own receipt; later missing supplies or a changed purse do not erase that history.
Ijale also runs a fruit shop. Buying an apple and giving her a beet are separate interactions, and buying fruit is not required for her request.
Ralg’s weapons and Bedgar’s armor have ordinary shop prices and availability. Descriptive stores elsewhere in the village need their own service integration before they become trade objectives.
Bean, beet and wheat farms show field work, fences, barns and family chores. Visiting these places or defeating pests does not by itself record a useful contribution to a farm.
Livestock, pets and horses have different roles. Working horses, riding horses and a stable keeper do not establish an accepted animal-care, riding or delivery quest.
The wizard’s hill house, servant, wood golem and imp provide a household story to explore. Descriptive books and inventions are not automatically items, lessons or useful spell outcomes.
Soldiers and their captain are investigating the woods. A guard and a gate stand on a route, but permission, answers and a lasting resolution need explicit integration.
The pond offers water when its stock remains. Drinking, filling a container, caring for wildlife and restoring a water source are different outcomes.
The faerie ring, brook, woodlands and rocky paths offer landmarks. Their stories need accepted knowledge, actual route admission and useful results before further achievements are added.

Swamp creatures, caves, the troll burrow and the rock plateau have their own dangers and native movement rules. Atmospheric descriptions alone do not certify swimming, falling, rescue or safe shelter.

The builder plan covers wider farm, family, wildlife, investigation and guidance stories. Additional journal objectives will appear when their successful actions and lasting outcomes are specifically integrated.
